text:
drew: quick heads-up — hit a repro where cancelling the context for a generator stream in the sampleapp doesn't stop the background auth/retry goroutine. CPU and goroutines climb after repeated cancels.
shreya: can you share the minimal repro and SDK version?
drew: using go-sdk v0.12.1 and the gen-sample app from `examples/gen-sample`. repro: run `./gen-sample --stream` then cancel after first token.
drew: code snippet (minimal):
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 5*time.Second)
defer cancel()
client := redwood.NewClient("$API_KEY")
iter, err := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
for iter.Next() {
  fmt.Println(iter.Token())
}
if err := iter.Err(); err != nil { log.Println("iter err:", err) }
```
shreya: looks fine on its face — are you calling `iter.Close()` or `client.Close()` after cancel?
drew: I assumed cancel would be enough; calling `iter.Close()` helps but the leak still happens. after cancel I see many auth refresh logs and a stuck goroutine:
```
2026-03-22T14:01:12Z auth: refresh queued (req id=abc123)
2026-03-22T14:01:12Z stream: ctx canceled, waiting for auth loop to finish
2026-03-22T14:01:13Z auth: retry attempt 1 (req id=abc123)
```
kai: probable cause: auth refresher spawns a background retry goroutine that doesn't observe the request ctx — it watches a global token refresh channel instead. if the stream ctx is canceled the auth loop keeps retrying and re-enqueues work.
morgan: can you run with `GODEBUG=gctrace=1` and `pprof` to dump goroutines? that'll show stuck stacks. also try the workaround: create client with a short-lived auth context bound to the request ctx, e.g. `authClient.WithContext(ctx)` (if available) or wrap the transport to check ctx.Done().
drew: attaching the goroutine stack (trimmed):
```
goroutine 4510 [chan receive]:
net/http.(*persistConn).writeLoop(...)
github.com/redwood/sdk/auth.(*Refresher).runRetryLoop(0xc000...)
created by github.com/redwood/sdk/auth.(*Refresher).Start
```
shreya: thanks — I can reproduce locally with `examples/gen-sample` and a tight timeout. filing an issue now: RED-ISSUE-2747. suggested fix: make the auth refresher accept a child ctx per request so retries select on ctx.Done() and stop.
kai: small PR queued in my fork to add `select { case <-reqCtx.Done(): return }` in the retry loop + ensure `iter.Close()` triggers a cancel on the per-request auth ctx. will open a draft.
drew: nice. for onboarding docs, we should call out that streaming generators need explicit Close() and mention auth edgecases in the quickstart — caught a lot of folks by surprise.
ciara-bot: CI status: draft PR created at https://github.com/redwood/inference/pull/891 (ci: pending).
shreya: adding a short note to devex quickstart and the sampleapp README about `defer iter.Close()` and cancellation patterns. can someone review my wording?
morgan: happy to review — also add a tiny example showing `ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background()); go func(){ time.Sleep(2*time.Second); cancel() }()` so people can see cancel behavior in tests.
drew: thanks all — saved me a lot of time. will test the draft PR once CI finishes. :thumbsup:
